The framework introduces two architectures: Block-Wise LoRA-MoE with centralized routing and Cell-Wise LoRA-MoE with decentralized, autonomous gating at the matrix cell level. Extensive testing across various benchmarks, including matrix simulations, tabular data transformations, and vision tasks under sensor degradation, shows that both architectures effectively resolve optimization deadlocks found in static models. Notably, the decentralized cell-level gating matches the performance of a global coordinator, providing a robust mechanism to prevent gradient corruption. These results demonstrate that Localized LoRA-MoE offers a scalable, parameter-efficient solution for dynamic adaptation in complex and changing operational environments.

item.title: Researchers introduce noisy channel decomposition of Minimum Bayes Risk decoding to incorporate bidirectional effects and improve text generation evaluation metrics [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a noisy channel decomposition of Minimum Bayes Risk (MBR) decoding to address asymmetries in text generation evaluation metrics like BLEU and COMET. This approach incorporates bidirectional effects by breaking down MBR decoding into four components: hypothesis-to-reference likelihood, reference-to-hypothesis likelihood, hypothesis prior, and reference prior. This decomposition offers a unified view of existing MBR methods and enhances interpretability by isolating each channel's contribution. The study's analysis shows that these channel contributions vary across different metrics but remain consistent across tasks, suggesting that adjusting channel weights could improve upon traditional MBR decoding. This advancement aims to produce more robust and higher-quality text generation by better aligning hypothesis selection with the characteristics of common evaluation metrics.

item.title: Researchers propose HeRo, a selective disclosure watermarking framework for large language models enabling fine-grained metadata access control with high detection accuracy and low latency [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed HeRo, a new watermarking framework for large language models that enables selective disclosure of embedded metadata. Unlike existing multi-bit watermarking methods that require revealing the entire embedded message for verification, HeRo allows different verifiers to access only specific portions of the watermark based on their access level. This approach enhances privacy by preventing unnecessary information exposure while maintaining high detection accuracy and low latency. HeRo works by recursively partitioning the vocabulary and distributing watermark information across hierarchical layers, preserving the unbiased nature of the text generation process and ensuring text quality. Experiments demonstrate that this method supports fine-grained access control without compromising the underlying sampling process. The researchers have made the code publicly available for further exploration and use.

item.title: Researchers introduce GaP, a multi-agent Graph-as-Policy system for variational automation tasks, achieving higher success rates in simulation and real-world benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed GaP, a multi-agent Graph-as-Policy system designed to improve robot performance in Variational Automation (VA) tasks, which involve significant variations in object geometry and pose. GaP constructs directed computation graphs from a Modular Open Robot Skill Library and uses internal simulations to iteratively refine these graphs, enhancing success rates and throughput. Evaluations on eight new VA task benchmarks, both in simulation and real-world settings, demonstrate that GaP significantly outperforms existing baseline methods. The system integrates perception, planning, and control nodes to create adaptable and interpretable robot programming, addressing the limitations of model-free policies in commercial and industrial applications. By rehearsing multiple task instances in parallel within a simulated environment, GaP effectively optimizes its policy graphs for persistent and reliable task execution. The researchers have made their code, data, and detailed results publicly available online for further exploration and development.

item.title: Researchers derive continuous-time Markov chain ELBO for discrete diffusion models, proving the Oracle Distance theorem and identifying optimizer coordinates across denoiser, score, and bridge plug-in predictors [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have derived a continuous-time Markov chain evidence lower bound (ELBO) for discrete diffusion models, establishing the Oracle Distance theorem which states that the negative ELBO equals the data entropy plus the path KL divergence from the oracle reverse process to the learned one. This result identifies the unique optimizer as the conditional expectation of the true reverse jump rate given the current noisy state, showing that all noising processes share the same optimal negative ELBO equal to the data entropy. The study further reveals that for sequences with token-factorizing noise, the optimizer can be expressed in three exact coordinates-denoiser, cavity (bridge plug-in), and score-with closed-form conversions among them. This framework clarifies which loss functions in existing literature correspond to which optimization laws, explains differences between masked and uniform diffusion, and addresses issues such as ELBO divergence at initialization under certain parameterizations. All theoretical identities were numerically verified on an exactly solvable model without approximation.

item.title: Researchers introduce LLM-as-a-Verifier, a general-purpose framework providing fine-grained verification and continuous scoring for agentic tasks, achieving state-of-the-art results on multiple benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed LLM-as-a-Verifier, a versatile verification framework that enhances the ability of large language models (LLMs) to assess the correctness of solutions in agentic tasks. This framework generates continuous scores by computing expectations over scoring token logits, allowing for fine-grained feedback without additional training. It improves verification accuracy by scaling score granularity, repeated evaluation, and criteria decomposition, and achieves state-of-the-art results on several benchmarks including Terminal-Bench V2, SWE-Bench Verified, RoboRewardBench, and MedAgentBench. The approach introduces a cost-efficient ranking algorithm to select the best candidate solutions based on continuous scores and provides detailed signals that can estimate task progress. An extension for Claude Code has been developed to help developers monitor and enhance their agentic systems. Additionally, LLM-as-a-Verifier offers dense feedback for reinforcement learning, boosting sample efficiency in robotics and mathematical reasoning tasks.

item.title: Researchers propose Direct On-Policy Distillation to transfer reinforcement learning policy shifts from smaller to stronger models, boosting Qwen3-1.7B performance on AIME 2024 by 14 percentage points in 4 hours [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced Direct On-Policy Distillation (Direct-OPD), a method to transfer reinforcement learning (RL) policy improvements from smaller, less costly models to stronger, more complex ones. This approach addresses the challenge of expensive RL training on large models by leveraging the policy shifts learned by smaller models and applying them as implicit rewards to enhance the performance of larger models without retraining from scratch. Using Direct-OPD, the team significantly improved the Qwen3-1.7B model's performance on the AIME 2024 benchmark, increasing accuracy from 48.3% to 62.4% within four hours on eight A100 GPUs. Direct-OPD works by comparing a smaller model's policy before and after RL training, using the difference as a dense reward signal for the larger model's own on-policy states. This technique bypasses the need for explicit reward models or sparse-reward RL on the target model, enabling efficient reuse of RL supervision across model scales. The method outperforms traditional direct RL approaches and supports sequential application of multiple policy shifts, demonstrating a scalable way to generalize RL improvements from weak to strong models.

item.title: Researchers propose Iterative Value Refinement, an evolutionary framework to improve value-guided decoding for large language models, reducing computational costs and enhancing alignment across tasks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced Iterative Value Refinement, an evolutionary framework designed to enhance value-guided decoding in large language models. This approach addresses the limitations of existing methods that rely on static value functions trained on narrow data, by using Value Exploration and Iterative Self-Refinement to generate more accurate value functions and higher-quality training data. The framework improves alignment across tasks such as text summarization, multi-turn dialogue, and instruction following while significantly reducing computational costs. The method works by iteratively refining the value function: each improved iteration guides the generation of better data for subsequent training, thereby narrowing the distributional gap that hampers current value-guided decoding techniques. Extensive experiments demonstrate that this approach not only achieves better alignment but also offers a more efficient and effective way to control language model outputs without retraining the models.

item.title: Researchers introduce Context Tuning to improve few-shot adaptation of large language models without weight updates, outperforming in-context learning and prompt-based methods on multiple benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Context Tuning, a novel method to improve few-shot adaptation of large language models (LLMs) without updating their weights. Unlike traditional in-context learning, which forms a fixed memory representation from demonstrations, Context Tuning initializes a trainable memory from these demonstrations and refines it through gradient-based optimization. This approach outperforms both in-context learning and prompt-based adaptation methods across multiple benchmarks, including CrossFit, UnifiedQA, MMLU, BIG-Bench Hard, and ARC. Context Tuning leverages the inherent in-context learning ability of LLMs to create a more effective and adaptable memory representation. It achieves competitive accuracy with test-time training methods while offering significantly higher training efficiency, making it a promising advancement for enhancing LLM performance in few-shot learning scenarios.

item.title: Researchers introduce Parity-aware Byte Pair Encoding to reduce tokenization inequality across languages by up to 89% with minimal impact on compression and language model performance [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Parity-aware Byte Pair Encoding (BPE), a new variant of the widely-used BPE tokenization algorithm, to address inequalities in tokenization across languages. Traditional tokenizers often favor dominant languages in training data, resulting in longer and less efficient tokenizations for lower-resource languages, which increases computational and financial disparities. Parity-aware BPE introduces a fair-max rule at each merge step to maximize compression gains for the worst-compressed language, significantly reducing tokenization inequality by up to 89% compared to classical BPE. This approach achieves improved cross-lingual fairness with minimal impact on overall compression rates and no observed degradation in downstream language model performance. By balancing tokenization efficiency across languages, Parity-aware BPE aims to promote more equitable natural language processing for diverse linguistic communities.
